title: RHABDOMYOSARCOMA (RMS): AN ORBITAL OVERVIEW
summary: A comprehensive guide to Rhabdomyosarcoma, the most common primary orbital malignancy in childhood. This poster details the demographics, histopathological subtypes, diagnostic signs, and current treatment protocols including IRSG guidelines.

sections.title: Introduction & Demographics
content: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is the most common soft tissue sarcoma of childhood.
40% develop in the head and neck.
It is the most common primary orbital malignancy in children but is still a rare condition.
Approximately 90% occur in children under 16 years.
The average age of onset is 7 years.

sections.title: Clinical Diagnosis: Signs & Symptoms
content: Symptoms: Rapidly progressive unilateral proptosis is usual.
Tumour Location: Most commonly superonasal or superior (Fig. 4.42B).
Alternative Locations: May arise anywhere in the orbit, including inferiorly (Fig. 4.42C), conjunctiva, and uvea.
Skin Signs: Swelling and redness develop (not warm).
Sensory: Diplopia is frequent.
Sensory: Pain is less common.

sections.title: Diagnostic Investigations
content: MRI: Shows a poorly defined mass.
CT: Shows a poorly defined mass of homogeneous density, often with adjacent bony destruction (Fig. 4.42D).
Incisional Biopsy: Performed to confirm diagnosis, establish histopathological subtype, and cytogenetic characteristics.
Systemic Investigation: Should be performed for metastasis (most common sites: lung and bone).

sections.title: Treatment Protocols
sections.content: Commonly used guidelines for staging and a corresponding treatment protocol were produced by the Intergroup Rhabdomyosarcoma Study Group (IRSG). Treatment encompasses a combination of radiotherapy, chemotherapy and sometimes surgical debulking. A single oncogenic fusion gene is associated with treatment resistance and a 40–45% decrease in overall survival. Entinostat with chemotherapy may improve the prognosis in selected cases of rhabdomyosarcoma, but has not yet been approved for clinical use.

content.explanation: The prognosis for patients with disease confined to the orbit is good.
